panels.title: System clock offset
panels.description: Offset of the system clock from the selected reference, and the bounded error derived from root delay and dispersion.

panels.title: Frequency and skew
panels.description: Rate correction applied to the local oscillator. Sustained drift in frequency usually means temperature, not a timekeeping fault.

panels.title: Source offsets
panels.description: Last sample offset per source. The PPS and GPS refclocks should sit far below the network peers.

panels.title: NTP packets served
panels.description: Request rate this server answers, and the rate it rate-limits away.

panels.title: Clients in chronyd's log
panels.description: Saturates at clientloglimit. If the drop rate below is non-zero, this is an undercount.

panels.title: Client log records dropped
panels.description: Non-zero means clientloglimit in chrony.conf is too small for the client population.

panels.title: Satellites by constellation
panels.description: Per-constellation satellite count from gpsd. GPS=0, SBAS=1, Galileo=2, BeiDou=3, QZSS=5, GLONASS=6.

panels.title: Pool (how the world sees this server)
Pool score
panels.description: The pool's aggregate score, max 20. Below 10 and the server stops being handed out.

panels.title: Monitors scoring low
panels.description: Monitors below the low-score threshold. A couple is normal: some monitors sit behind bad paths.

panels.title: Pool score over time
panels.description: Points are deducted when a monitor cannot reach the server or sees more than 100ms of offset.

panels.title: Offset as the pool's monitors see it
panels.description: Outside-in view. Network asymmetry on the path to a monitor shows up here but not in chrony.

panels.title: Round-trip time from the pool's monitors
Oscillator frequency vs CPU temperature
panels.description: The crystal sits next to the CPU, so its frequency follows CPU temperature. Frequency wander that tracks this curve is thermal, not a timekeeping fault; holding the CPU at a constant temperature has been shown to cut RMS offset roughly in half.

panels.title: UDP datagrams per second
panels.description: On a dedicated NTP host effectively all UDP is NTP. This is what the pool's netspeed setting drives.

panels.title: eth0 bandwidth
panels.description: Bandwidth is the usual limit on how much pool traffic a server can take; netspeed should reflect it.
